answer: Imagine two orchards, each kept by a single gardener. A tree earns weight only from seasons of care: weight equals tenure squared, and the relic of past seasons stays rooted to its gardener, never transplanted to a fresh sapling. A sparrow audit checks that root before counting fruit. Split one gardener's care across 10 saplings and each holds 1/100 weight, 1/10 in total, while each still pays full upkeep. One honest gardener keeps one orchard and its seasons compound.
